explain.narrative:
## Java Annotations

Annotations provide metadata for compilers, tools and runtime frameworks. Custom annotations use @interface; retention and target control where they apply.

Identify the input and desired result. Select the Java construct or API that supports the requirement. Keep code readable, handle documented failures and state assumptions clearly.

Compile with JDK 21, predict output before running, and test normal, boundary and invalid inputs.

examples.title: Core concept
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { System.out.println(Deprecated.class.isAnnotation()); } }
examples.explanation: Shows that Deprecated is an annotation type.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { class Example { @Override public String toString() { return "Example"; } } System.out.println(new Example()); } }
examples.explanation: Uses Override so the compiler checks the method override.

examples.title: Boundary behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { @SuppressWarnings("deprecation") String oldName = "legacy"; System.out.println(oldName); } }
examples.explanation: Shows a narrowly scoped suppression example.

examples.title: Alternative pattern
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { @java.lang.annotation.Retention(java.lang.annotation.RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME) @interface Marker {} @Marker class Marked {} System.out.println(Marked.class.isAnnotationPresent(Marker.class)); } }
examples.explanation: A custom annotation with runtime retention can be inspected through reflection.

examples.title: Verify the result
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { @java.lang.annotation.Target(java.lang.annotation.ElementType.TYPE) @interface CourseTag {} @CourseTag class Course {} System.out.println(Course.class.isAnnotationPresent(CourseTag.class)); } }
examples.explanation: A custom annotation with default CLASS retention is not visible through runtime reflection.

practise.guidedTask: Use @Override and @Deprecated in a small example. Declare a custom runtime annotation with @Target(TYPE), apply it to a class and inspect it with reflection.
practise.independentTask: Create a custom annotation with documented retention and target. Demonstrate how a runtime-retained annotation can be read with reflection.
hints: Use the API's documented contract rather than relying on assumptions.
Keep examples minimal and demonstrate one behavior at a time.
Compile with JDK 21 and verify both present and absent or failure cases.
practise.challenge: Compare SOURCE, CLASS and RUNTIME retention. Explain why SuppressWarnings should be narrow and why annotations are metadata rather than automatic behavior.
